subject: Performance goals alignment + integration checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@clearmap.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance goals alignment + integration checklist

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

Key pain points you raised:
- Bursty streaming workload for live transcription/summary (peaks ~1.4k concurrent streams).
- Hard p95 latency requirement: <= 350ms for first-token on live audio-to-text pipeline.
- Tail latency variability when long sessions hit 8k+ tokens (KV cache pressure).
- Cost sensitivity for inference: want predictable unit economics for 10M tokens/month baseline.

Current stack & constraints you shared:
- Real-time ingestion via Kafka -> custom audio chunker -> in-house preproc -> HTTP calls to models.
- Currently using a managed LLM endpoint (third-party) with limited streaming support; no KV cache reuse across sessions.
- Authentication via Okta, corp VPC; procurement requires SOC2 evidence and an inbound firewall rule list.

Success criteria you care about (stated):
1) First-token p95 under 350ms for 99% of streams at target concurrency.
2) End-to-end streaming UX with incremental partial responses (no 5–10s buffering).
3) Clear fallback behavior when capacity constrained (graceful degrade to smaller model or chunked responses).
4) Total inference cost <= target (you mentioned $/1k tokens goal, will confirm range).

Our immediate proposal / ask from you:
- Redwood will provide a short scoped POC: dedicated 2-week run with a small fleet (reserved) to validate p95 and streaming UX.
- We’ll measure first-token latency, sustained throughput, and tail behavior using a replay of a 24-hour window you can share (sample data).
- Need a sample of 500 representative sessions (audio -> tokenized input lengths and typical session durations) and a short whiteboard of your ingestion flow (Kafka topics, chunk sizes).

Action items / timeline (proposed):
- You: share sample session traces + contact for procurement (Victor) and security (procurement@clearmap.ai) — due Wed 6/17.
- Redwood (Marissa): provide integration checklist and quick infra diagram — by Fri 6/19.
- Redwood (Ben): draft POC cost estimate and reserved capacity options — by Mon 6/22.
- Joint: 2-week POC kickoff target week of 6/29 if approvals complete.

Attachments: I attached a one-page integration checklist and a preliminary architecture diagram (redwood-arch-v1.pdf).

If that all matches your understanding, reply-all with any corrections and we’ll lock the kickoff dates.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@clearmap.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Ramos <victor.ramos@clearmap.ai>, procurement@clearmap.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance goals alignment + integration checklist

Thanks Aditya — that summary looks accurate. A few clarifications and a tweak on priorities: 

Clarifications:
- Concurrency: peaks are spiky; sustained concurrency is ~400, but we see microbursts up to ~1.4k for 30–90s windows. Those bursts are the main source of tail latency.
- p95: our internal target for first-token is actually <= 300ms, but we can accept <=350ms for the POC if the tails are well understood.
- Token lengths: average session 1.2k tokens, ~10% go beyond 8k tokens (those are long meetings).

Procurement & security: I’ve looped in Victor and procurement@clearmap.ai — Victor will own SOC2 evidence requests and firewall rules. Expect a short vendor questionnaire; procurement will share the link tomorrow.

Data for POC: I can share a 48-hour replay dump (anonymized) and a separate CSV of session length distribution. Due to privacy we’ll strip PII. I’ll upload to your Drive link by Wed 6/17 EOD.

Next steps from our side:
- Victor: will follow up w/ the vendor questionnaire and a point on allowed egress IP ranges.
- Procurement: will review POC terms (duration, liability caps) and request a standard SOW.

Happy to proceed with the proposed timeline. Confirming we want the POC to focus on: streaming first-token latency, incremental partial response UX, and fallback behavior for model swap.

Appreciate the clear action items — I’ll reply once Victor confirms procurement timeline.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Product | ClearMap AI
sofia@clearmap.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance goals alignment + integration checklist (ClearMap POC prep)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the thread from ClearMap. Highlights and asks: 

- Priority: streaming first-token latency (ClearMap wants <=300ms target; will accept <=350ms for POC).
- Workload shape: sustained ~400 conc, bursts to 1.4k for short windows, ~10% long sessions >8k tokens.
- Security/procurement: Victor + procurement@clearmap.ai will own the questionnaire and firewall/egress IP list. 

Marissa: please finalize the integration checklist (I attached redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx). We need a short runbook for the POC (who patches, metrics we’ll collect, required logs).
Ben: can you produce two scoped pricing options: 1) Reserved mini-fleet for 2 weeks (SLA-lite) and 2) On-demand with scaling to absorb bursts. Include an estimate of token cost and an explicit line for short-lived burst capacity.

I expect procurement to push some SOW terms — I’ll loop you both into those threads as they appear. Let me know if you want to triage now; otherwise I’ll reconvene early next week.

Thanks,
Aditya
